answer.rationale: A release went out two hours ago, and the p99 write-path latency climbed to 5× target within a 90-minute window that overlaps the post-deploy period. Memory b1 records that rolling back a release cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact, and memory b5 shows that offloading read work to replicas freed the primary and restored write latency. Because writes are heavy at settlement peak, rolling back directly removes the suspected cause of the degradation. Read-replica routing is the next intervention if latency does not recover, but only one action is allowed in this window.
